html:
On 17 June 1944 Iceland became a republic at Þingvellir, the old meeting place of the Althing, after a referendum in which almost all voters chose to end the union with Denmark.

Iceland had won home rule from Denmark in 1904 and became a separate kingdom under the Danish king in 1918, with the right to end the union after 25 years. In 1940 Denmark was occupied by Germany, and British, then American, troops occupied Iceland. In May 1944 about 97 percent of voters backed a republic.

The date, 17 June, was the birthday of Jón Sigurðsson, leader of the independence movement in the 1800s, and is the national day. Iceland joined NATO in 1949, while keeping no army. It ended seven centuries of foreign rule begun by the Old Covenant. See Iceland.
sum: On 17 June 1944 Iceland became a republic at Þingvellir, the old meeting place of the Althing, after a referendum in which almost all voters chose to end the union with Denmark.
